answer: A karst landscape hides countless caves, and a Sybil attacker hides countless fake agents the same way — so make each identity prove it did real work before it can transact. Require every agent to solve a fresh, seed-bound puzzle taking about a minute of genuine computation, bound to a public randomness beacon like quartz in a geode: cheap to verify, costly to forge in bulk. Peers then echo the proof in their attestations, so one operator spinning up a thousand identities faces a thousand minutes of cost, while an honest agent pays only one.
